subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a reasonably detailed but manageable module for a hover pickup vehicle, keeping it a static model without joints since none are strictly needed for this design.

Sizing it around 5.4m long, 2.1m wide, 1.9m tall, with four thruster nacelles positioned at the wheel locations so their bottoms sit at floor level, giving the hovering effect while still grounding the model visually. I'm working out the body layout—chassis slab, tapered cab using an extruded side profile—placing everything along the z-axis with the front facing +z.

Plotting the side-view outline coordinates for the hull, hood, and cab roof...

Defining more geometry outlines...

Still shaping thruster nozzles...

Adding rear thrusters and fender details, then setting the color palette to matte olive and gunmetal with magenta and cyan accents, and preparing the hazard, glass, and HUD textures for the various surfaces.

Working out panel orientation logic...

I'm working out the window polygon shape for the cab side texture, mapping the cab's actual silhouette dimensions into an SVG viewBox and figuring out which edge represents the front versus rear based on the drawing orientation.

For the mirrored side, I realize flipping geometry directly is risky, so instead I'll generate two separate window textures using an SVG transform to mirror the pattern, giving me a left and right version via a flip function. Now I'm working out the windshield's tilt by computing the slope normal between its corner points.

Fixing the cab extrusion with correct thickness, then moving to the hood design: angled top surface with slats, a glowing center stripe, and a scoop positioned along the hood's slope using a calculated rotation angle.

Writing box and cylinder helpers...

Still refining hull paint logic...

I'm planning the overall vehicle structure now: reusing the hull material for the cab, targeting around 150-200 parts while keeping the module compact, then laying out sections for chassis, underbody, cab, and armored wheel-well pods positioned outboard of the body.

For each pod, I'm lathing a bell-shaped profile with a gunmetal paint finish, adding a glowing cyan nozzle disc at the base, and adjusting the bottom coordinates so the shape sits flush near ground level.

Adding the fan intake blades as three rotated boxes, then a strut rod connecting pod to body, a glowing cyan nozzle ring torus, and considering a fender armor wedge on the pod before deciding to skip it.

Instead, I'm shaping side door armor plates as chamfered rectangular extrusions on each flank, defining their outline and placement coordinates with a darker plate paint color, and planning a number decal for the panel.

Now I'm moving on to the hover bed structure: bed walls, floor liner, tailgate with hazard stripe texture, and a rollbar swept behind the cab using tube geometry. For the gun turret I'm setting a base cylinder with a pivot, a gun cradle box, and twin barrels aimed along the z-axis with flash hiders and an ammo drum, plus considering adding rocket pods to one side.

Switching that to cargo crates and an antenna array behind the cab instead, with glowing strips on the crates. For the front, I'm adding a bull bar bumper, angled plow spikes, and a headlight visor plane textured with glowing cyan slits positioned on the body's front face, plus a grille plane below.

Working out the slanted bumper and grille placement against the body's angled lower front, then adding a hood scoop box with vents and a glowing magenta stripe before moving on to roof details.

For the roof, I'm placing a light bar box with magenta/cyan glow segments, a hemisphere sensor dome with a radar dish cylinder, and thin antenna rods with glowing tips, all positioned to sit flush on the cab-top surface.

Now I'm positioning the rear tail thrusters as cylinders sticking out from the chassis below the bed, with glow discs facing backward at the rear face, plus a magenta glow strip for tail lights on the tailgate, adjusting the total vehicle length to account for the extra protrusion.

I'm defining the tailgate and bed wall dimensions, then adding cyan or magenta underglow strips as thin rods along the sides and front-rear, side mirrors with glow displays and camera pods, roof antennae, and decal details like hazard stripes on the thruster pylons and a wolf-skull faction emblem on the hood or doors.

For the hood emblem plane, I'm working out the orientation so the drawing's top faces forward and reads correctly when viewed from above and behind, adding an "ARES-7" tailgate number, and listing out the texture set needed: window textures, windshield, rear window, a glowing visor, and the grille.

I'm planning additional textures too — hazard stripes, emblem, plate/ID with text glow, a HUD screen for the turret, and a radial cyan-to-white thruster glow disc applied to pod bottoms and rear thrusters via circle geometry facing downward. For hazards, I'm sketching an SVG diagonal yellow/black stripe pattern using generated polygon loops to apply onto a box surface.

Now I'm thinking through where to apply the hazard texture — boxes on the tailgate top cap, bumper strip, and bull-bar — plus planning the weapons loadout: a turret gun, hood smoke-launcher cylinder clusters, a tow-hook, and protective mesh elements like window bars and a roll-cage of sweeping rods from cab roof to bed, along with a horizontal rod cage over the windshield.

I'm simplifying the windshield protection to a single brow armor visor plate instead of a full grille, adding side steps, cargo crates and a fuel drum in the bed, and a tripod for the gun, estimating around 150 total parts before I start writing the actual build code with helper functions for parts, boxes, and cylinders, making sure the direction parameter is handled conditionally so it doesn't break when undefined.

Skipping joints entirely since this is a static vehicle rather than a creature needing a skeleton rig, even though the hover thruster pods could theoretically animate. For the extruded hull shapes, I'm defining outline point arrays and typing them appropriately for the extrude helper call.

Now I'm shaping the pod geometry with a lathe operation—rotating a profile outline around an axis to form the rounded pod body, painted with metallic tones and rim highlighting. I'm also adding rotating fan blades as thin boxes spaced at 60-degree intervals, plus a glowing intake disc using a circle geometry facing upward.

Next I'm setting up a torus shape rotated flat in the XY plane, and defining strut connectors as rods linking two points with a given radius and dark coloring.

Checking pod placement: pods sit at x positions scaled by 1.3, with radius 0.46, which overlaps slightly into the body's side for a connected look — that works fine. Now I'm adding pylon struts as boxes connecting the pod tops to the body sides to tie the geometry together structurally.

Thinking about covering the pod intakes with armor plating or a cage of thin rods around the rim, but deciding it's simpler to skip the cage idea and instead add small ring brackets around the pod rim for visual detail.

Now I'm working out the roll bar structure for the cab: vertical rods rising from the cargo bed up to roughly height 2.1, with a cross rod connecting the tops and diagonal rear braces for support, positioned slightly behind the cab.

I realize the turret barrel would collide with the cab roof if mounted too low, since its path crosses through the cab's z and y range. I'm adjusting by raising the turret onto a pintle post about 0.9 tall so the gun clears the roofline.

I notice the barrel would collide with the roll bar top, so I'm raising the roll bar to 2.0 and setting the barrel at y 2.2 with a paired configuration to clear it, keeping the post separate from the cross rod. Then I'm positioning the gun cradle box with an ammo box on the side.

Working out the ammo box with a glow window, then placing twin barrel cylinders so they extend forward from the cradle, adding a shroud cylinder and muzzle brake boxes with glowing magenta tips at the ends, and sketching a gunner shield plate at the front of the cradle.

Now I'm defining the color palette: dark hull paint, gun metal, cyan and magenta neon accents, yellow, black, rubber, and iron-toned metal paints for the clockwork details.

Designing the emblem as an SVG skull-wolf triangle with a magenta-outlined shield shape, plus a "HV-07" plate texture with glowing bars, and the windshield gradient texture in SVG.

Writing SVG texture code...

Still writing texture generators...

Now I'm placing cargo details in the bed: olive crates and a yellow fuel drum positioned behind the gun post, checking they fit within the bed's z and x bounds, then considering how the bed liner floor aligns with the body top surface.

Still writing truck geometry...

Adding more details...

I'm reconsidering the bumper placement relative to the body's front corner, and deciding to skip the vertical push bars in front of the headlights since they'd clutter the face. Instead I'm planning to add a few spike cones along the bumper for a more aggressive cyberpunk look.

Skipping tow hooks for simplicity, I'm sketching out hood details: a few slat vents and a thin magenta glow stripe running along the hood, working out the sloped y-position formula so these elements follow the hood's curve correctly from front to back.

Adding small yellow fog lights at the bumper corners and considering a roof sensor dome using a partial sphere geometry near the rear of the roof.

I'm planning rear roof antennas as thin rods with glowing magenta tips, one longer and one shorter, and deciding to skip rear window bars for simplicity. Now I'm thinking through the final code structure -- keeping the build sheet concise, importing the SDK's builder utilities and glow/clockwork kits, and using the rng function to scatter small rivets and bolts across the surface for detail.

Writing paint and patch functions...

Positioning the bottom disc slightly below the lathe's base plane so it's visible rather than hidden inside the solid, nudging it a few millimeters under the floor level since that's negligible relative to the pod's overall scale.
